content.comment_body: Hello. I have a network of 4 [product_name] connected via Ethernet. I have assigned IPs to each and loaded their programs. In simulation, remote outputs work, but in reality, they do not. I believe the issue may be with client/server or master/slave configuration. Can someone assist? Thank you.
If you intend to run a standalone program on each of the 4 [product_name], do not set them as slaves. A slave device does not run a program but simply provides hardware information to the master.
So, should I configure all 4 devices as clients?

All four devices can exchange data with each other. Setting up a server/client connection is the simplest method. If you use multi-window mode for diagrams, you can drag connections between diagrams, and the software will automatically generate the connections and connection lists.

I haven't made changes to the network, and I don't understand why I needed to change the subnet of the [product_name]. Could the issue be with the switch? It's odd since I was able to program using the switch, which runs at 100Mbps and transmits signals from [product_name] and acts as a hub. Thanks.
I'm unclear about your issue. What exactly isn't working? Is it the transfer to the device or the communication between devices?
It is the communication between the devices.
Could you upload your project to the forum as a zipped attachment?
The subnet mask setting is incorrect.

The first device has a different subnet mask compared to the other 3 devices. All devices should have identical subnet masks. Are they connected through a router or directly to the PC? The gateway address should be the router’s IP if a router is present; otherwise, you can leave it blank.
Thank you. I am heading to the construction site to begin the setup.

analysis.insight_summary: Users successfully run simulations of remote outputs with multiple [product_name] devices on an Ethernet network, but face communication problems during actual deployment. The main issue is discovered to be a network configuration error, specifically with the subnet mask settings, rather than hardware or software faults from the devices. There is also confusion about configuring the correct networking roles for these devices and the impact of hardware like switches.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] devices to communicate via Ethernet as demonstrated in simulation software, and wants network roles and configuration to be straightforward and easy to apply.
